Eadrik was a worgen that served as Genn Greymane's messenger and loyal aide. He did various tasks for Genn, such as spying on the Highborne, whom Genn didn't seem to trust due to their reputation. Despite being told by Genn to leave the matter of the Highborne killings alone, he investigated them anyway and found out who the real killer was: Maiev Shadowsong. This however, put him and his followers in conflict with the Watchers, who have been trying to hunt him and his friends in order to silence them. Even so, he killed many of his assassins. The Dying Time is a period of orc history that lasted for three years and was one of its darkest. At this point in history the orcs were cut off from the elements, unable to connect to their ancestors as demons guarded the entrance to Oshu'gun, and corrupted all at the command Kil'jaeden. However instead of rewarding the orcs following the seemingly completed genocide of the draenei, Kil'jaeden instead abandoned them. With their world dying — the water supply was growing thin and diseased, combined with a decreasing number of animals due to the lack of grass — more orcs died of starvation and disease than any had during their war against the draenei. The European Computer Trade Show, commonly known as ECTS, was an annual trade show for the European computer and video game industry, which first ran in 1988, with the last event occurring in 2004. Echeyakee is a lion found in the Northern Barrens via summoning him for a Horde quest. His name means "Whitemist" in Taurahe. He will not be found wandering around if not summoned. During the Legion Invasion of Northern Barrens, Echeyakee was subdued by a dreadstalker, but was saved and bandaged. The beast then joined the adventurers and fought against the invading demons.

The term eat means the act of consuming a food item to regain health. Generally, a character must sit to eat as opposed to drinking, which can sometimes be done while standing or moving (as in the case of elixirs or potions).

An easter egg is an undocumented, obscure, or otherwise "hidden" command — usually buried deep within a program's source-code and only triggered by executing a certain series of actions or system commands. Often, an Easter egg will reveal an inside joke, though Easter eggs can also be placed into in-game props and scenery or only in areas visible to those that are actively using "cheat codes" (or otherwise circumventing the "normal" operation of the software). While Easter eggs were once included in virtually all computer software, software companies such as Microsoft have discontinued the practice, citing security concerns associated with undocumented (and often untested) code. Eastpoint Station is a ferry station located between Boralus and the settlement of Bridgeport in eastern Tiragarde Sound. It is the easternmost ferry point in the region outside the capital, and can be used to reach the nearby Greystone Keep and Ashvane Foundry. It also doubles as a small fishing center, with its own resident fishermen. The Ferry Master in charge of the station is Rosha Carrol.

Earthwatcher Shaman are tauren, orcs, Wildhammer dwarves, and draenei located in Shimmering Expanse.

Earthwatcher Waveguards are water elementals located in Shimmering Expanse and Kelp'thar Forest. They have been summoned by the Earthen Ring Shaman to fight off the Zin'jatar Fathom-Stalker. Along with the Greater Fire Elemental and the Greater Earth Elemental. They all are found dead after Fathom-Lord Zin'jatar cast on them. There is also one spawning in the Kelp'thar Forest near to Shallow's End to prevent PK'ing by 1-shooting.
Earthguard Sentinels are tauren located in Deepholm. They appear during On Even Ground.

The Eastern Dunes are a vast area in eastern Vol'dun, roughly covering most of the space between Atul'Aman in the southwest, the Withering Gulch in the south, the Blistering Wastes in the east, and Bonepicker Summit in the northeast. The region is mostly empty save for a few roaming krolusks.
